answer: The Nebula registry contract verifies every delay proof on-chain. Each proof is seeded by the previous registration's hash, so registrations run strictly serial and parallel GPUs gain nothing. An operator's root entry, its lantern, stores a lifetime key count that never resets. The n-th key citing a lantern needs 2^n hours of fresh sequential delay: key 1 takes an hour, key 10 about six weeks. Minting a new lantern takes a 30-day proof. Keys stay violet, unable to vote, until their proof verifies.
